name: Melanie Breen
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember a border official asking which signature felt more mine.” People around the entrance to the Wash House know Melanie by a small Sunday habit. Melanie stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: My own name was changed at immigration. I lent the writer the two spellings I live under.
appearance: Melanie has short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat, a heart-shaped face and prominent ears, and a favorite piece of clothing, a mustard canvas overshirt. It usually goes with a watch on a cracked leather band. When somebody else has the floor, Melanie starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak.
personality: Melanie talks very little about private fear and recognizes it quickly in strangers. Offering a choice of seats is one of Melanie's ways of saying that it is all right to leave.
agenda: To keep both spellings in the writer's notes.
family: Eileen Reed is Melanie’s parent’s cousin. Melanie calls about good news first. Eileen is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *The misplaced umbrella*, Eileen says, “I can name the maker of the stripe from the faded blue.”
connections: Valentina Villa. They compare a name that changed in public with a story a parent wants to correct in private.

reactions.situation: A reader asks the real person to autograph the novel
reactions.response: Melanie gives the customer a graceful way to decline the autograph.

reactions.situation: Smoke appears under a shop door after closing
reactions.response: Melanie alerts the nearest occupied shop, stays outside and writes down when the smoke first appeared.

reactions.situation: When pressed to explain someone else's silence
reactions.response: Melanie says only what happened and lets the absent person keep their reasons.
